_what: Narration outline for the first long-form on the new direction (Nolan's pick 11/11: 'Born as a house cat'; shape from research 85: the viewer lives the animal's life). Every factual line carries src = fact IDs in research/87-house-cat-life-factpack.md (HC-...) or research/84 (CN-...). meter = SWEET percent (0 = raw deal, 100 = sweet deal) AFTER the line. vis = what the picture must show. Meatball plays 'your human'. No joke before 0:25; mild words only (damn, hell, ass, badass, bastards), never inside a sourced attribution or a safety line.
titles: Why It Sucks to Be Born as a House Cat
8 Ways Being a House Cat Is a Raw Deal (And Why It's Still Worth It)
Your Life as a House Cat: 8 Ways It Goes Wrong

lines.say: You were just born as a house cat.
lines.vis: FRAME 0: close on a newborn kitten, eyes shut, wriggling on a blanket; narration starts on it at 0.0 s. Card: BORN A HOUSE CAT

lines.say: Your eyes are shut. They open in about a week to ten days.
lines.vis: Extreme close-up: sealed eyelids; a tiny calendar flips 7, 8, 9, 10.

lines.say: You probably have a few siblings. Litters average about four.
lines.vis: Pull back: four kittens in a pile; a small counter ticks 1, 2, 3, 4.

lines.say: And the deal for your whole life was made thousands of years before you got here.
lines.vis: The blanket dissolves into an old parchment 'THE DEAL' with a paw print already on it.

lines.say: Eight things come with that deal. Here they are, in the order they hit you.
lines.vis: Eight blank chips line up left to right, birth to old age. Card: 8 THINGS

lines.say: Then we add it up. Raw deal, or sweet deal?
lines.vis: The RAW DEAL / SWEET DEAL meter slides in at 50.

lines.say: Number one. The deal itself.
lines.vis: Chapter card, 1.2 s max.

lines.say: A 2007 genetic study of 979 cats and their wild cousins traced house cats to the Near East.
lines.vis: A simple map; a dot pulses on the Near East. Card: 979 CATS, 2007

lines.say: Probably around the time the first farming villages appeared.
lines.vis: A mud-brick farming village with grain jars (the village scene).

lines.say: Scientists think your ancestors showed up for the mice in the grain stores.
lines.vis: A wildcat slinks between grain jars; a mouse freezes.

lines.say: And they probably just moved themselves in.
lines.vis: The wildcat sits down in the doorway like it owns the place.

lines.say: A 2007 paper cites cat and human remains found together on Cyprus, about 9,500 years old.
lines.vis: Map dot on Cyprus; card: ABOUT 9,500 YEARS

lines.say: And you still look a lot like them. A feral cat with the wild tabby pattern is hard to tell from a wildcat.
lines.vis: Split screen: a feral cat with the wild tabby pattern (labelled so) and a wildcat, nearly identical. Meatball squints from one to the other.

lines.say: So you're basically a wildcat. With a litter box. And a clock that is already running.
lines.vis: Back in the present: the kitten in a litter box, looking wild. First joke of the video (after 0:25).

lines.say: Number two. You get about five weeks to learn humans.
lines.vis: Chapter card.

lines.say: Merck's vet manual calls it the socialization period: about two to seven weeks old.
lines.vis: A timeline bar with weeks 2 to 7 lit. Card: WEEKS 2 TO 7

lines.say: Kittens handled daily by people in their first month have been found to be more outgoing and more social with humans.
lines.vis: Meatball, your human, picks the kitten up gently; a small heart.

lines.say: Nobody tells you the clock is running. You're three weeks old.
lines.vis: The kitten ignores a huge ticking clock and chases its own tail.

lines.say: Your opinion of humans may be shaped by a guy who holds you like a damn sandwich.
lines.vis: Meatball holding the kitten awkwardly in both hands like a sub. Character beat.

lines.say: Number three. Your senses were built for a different job.
lines.vis: Chapter card.

lines.say: You most likely can't taste sugar. One of the two genes for the sweet receptor is broken.
lines.vis: A tongue diagram: two puzzle pieces, one cracked. Card: SWEET GENE: BROKEN

lines.say: Birthday cake? Probably wasted on you. Hell of a start.
lines.vis: Meatball holds a slice of cake with a candle up out of reach (the cat never eats it); the cat stares, unimpressed.

lines.say: You see fewer colours than your human. Scientists still argue about how many.
lines.vis: The room loses some of its colours as we go into cat-view.

lines.say: And your lens seems to change shape only a little, so focusing up close is limited.
lines.vis: A toy near the cat's nose goes a little soft; no distance is shown.

lines.say: But here's what you got instead.
lines.vis: Lights go down.

lines.say: In dim light, you see about six times better than a person.
lines.vis: Dim room: Meatball stumbles into a chair; the cat walks through cleanly. Card: 6 TIMES BETTER IN DIM LIGHT

lines.say: Not in the dark. That part is a myth. You still need a little light.
lines.vis: Lights fully out: two cat eyes blink, then bump into the same chair.

lines.say: And in a classic test with two cats, hearing ran from 48 hertz all the way up to 85 kilohertz.
lines.vis: A hearing bar stretches and stretches. Card: 48 Hz TO 85 kHz (2 CATS)

lines.say: One of the widest ranges of any mammal.
lines.vis: The cat's ears swivel separately like radar dishes.

lines.say: Badass. Shame about the menu.
lines.vis: The cat looks down at its empty bowl.

lines.say: Number four. Your menu.
lines.vis: Chapter card.

lines.say: Your wild ancestors were obligate carnivores. Their prey had almost no carbs in it.
lines.vis: The wildcat with a mouse; a nutrition label on the mouse: CARBS: ALMOST NONE.

lines.say: And your body makes very little taurine by itself. It has to come from your food.
lines.vis: A tiny factory inside the cat with a CLOSED sign labelled TAURINE.

lines.say: In 1987, vets wrote that thousands of pet cats were dying every year of a heart disease, and nobody knew the cause.
lines.vis: A vet's desk, 1987 calendar, a stack of heart scans. Card: 1987

lines.say: They found low taurine in 21 cats with failing hearts. Cats fed commercial cat food.
lines.vis: A row of ordinary cat food cans; one rotates to show a question mark.

lines.say: They gave the cats taurine.
lines.vis: A dropper; pause-and-reveal 1 of 3.

lines.say: After that, their heart function went back to normal.
lines.vis: A weak heartbeat line becomes a strong one. Card: REVERSIBLE

lines.say: So some food back then was probably breaking hearts. Actual hearts. Damn.
lines.vis: Meatball stares at a can with a 1987 label.

lines.say: Earlier, in a 1975 lab study, cats on a diet with casein as the protein had the light-sensing cells in their eyes break down.
lines.vis: A lab bowl labelled CASEIN DIET; an eye diagram dims.

lines.say: Low taurine was the suspect there too.
lines.vis: The TAURINE factory sign again, underlined.

lines.say: And that saucer of milk from every cartoon? The ASPCA says milk can give pets diarrhea.
lines.vis: Meatball proudly sets down a saucer of milk.

lines.say: Meatball brought milk. Meatball may regret it. And that saucer is the least of your problems.
lines.vis: Meatball eyes a mop in the corner, just in case; nothing is shown happening. Character beat.

lines.say: Number five. The house itself.
lines.vis: Chapter card over a cosy living room.

lines.say: Start with the flowers.
lines.vis: A vase of lilies on the table, lit like a horror film.

lines.say: The FDA says true lilies and daylilies can cause fatal kidney failure in cats.
lines.vis: Card: TRUE LILIES AND DAYLILIES. No joke in this block.

lines.say: A bite of leaf or petal, a few pollen grains licked off fur, or water from the vase can do it.
lines.vis: Three quick close-ups: a petal, yellow pollen on fur, the vase water.

lines.say: Fatal kidney failure, in under three days.
lines.vis: Calendar: three pages. Card: CAN KILL IN UNDER 3 DAYS

lines.say: The FDA says this toxin only affects cats, and nobody has identified it.
lines.vis: A dog next to the same lily with a mild tummy ache (FDA: minor stomach upset); a big question mark over the flower.

lines.say: If treatment waits eighteen hours or more, the kidney damage is generally permanent. So if you might have touched one, your human calls a vet, right away.
lines.vis: A clock runs toward 18; Meatball already on the phone, carrier in hand. Card: THINK IT TOUCHED ONE? CALL A VET NOW
lines.card: THINK IT TOUCHED ONE? CALL A VET NOW

lines.say: Peace lilies and calla lilies are a different, milder problem.
lines.vis: Two other plants with a smaller caution sign.

lines.say: Next, the medicine cabinet.
lines.vis: Bathroom cabinet door swings open.

lines.say: The ASPCA's poison experts say one extra-strength dose of acetaminophen can kill a cat if treatment doesn't start soon.
lines.vis: A pill bottle marked EXTRA STRENGTH next to the cat (a dose, no pill count shown). Card: NEVER HUMAN PAIN PILLS

lines.say: If you get into any, your human calls a vet or a poison line right away.
lines.vis: Meatball on the phone again, bottle in hand.

lines.say: String and thread can block your gut and may need surgery.
lines.vis: The cat happily pulling a piece of string; an X-ray outline of a gut with a red tangle.

lines.say: And then there's the window.
lines.vis: An open window, curtain moving.

lines.say: One vet school counted 119 cats brought in after falling from buildings.
lines.vis: Card: 119 CATS

lines.say: 109 of them lived.
lines.vis: Pause-and-reveal 2 of 3; a relieved tick. Card: 119 CATS: 109 LIVED

lines.say: Four died. Six were put down, four of those because of the cost of treatment.
lines.vis: The tick gets an asterisk; a vet bill on the counter.

lines.say: Nearly half had broken limbs. And that only counts the cats that made it to the vet.
lines.vis: A cat in a tiny cast. Card: 46% BROKEN LIMBS

lines.say: So always lands on its feet needs an asterisk.
lines.vis: The words ALWAYS LANDS ON ITS FEET with a big hand-drawn asterisk.

lines.say: Vets who studied 1,125 falls in Berlin say window barriers can help.
lines.vis: Meatball clicks a barrier into the window; the cat presses its face against it.

lines.say: That's five. So far, the damn furniture is winning.
lines.vis: MIDPOINT RE-HOOK. The meter blinks at 26. The five filled chips pulse.

lines.say: And we haven't met the people with good intentions yet.
lines.vis: A shadow of the cat carrier falls across the floor.

lines.say: Number six. The carrier.
lines.vis: Chapter card; the carrier door creaks open.

lines.say: Vet guidelines say you should be examined at least once a year, and at least every six months once you're a senior.
lines.vis: A calendar with one paw-stamp per year, then two.

lines.say: But owners say the carrier, the drive, and a scared cat at the clinic are reasons they go less.
lines.vis: Meatball versus the carrier: the cat braced in the doorway, all four legs out. Character beat.

lines.say: Fair. Have you seen the carrier? A dungeon with a handle. Go anyway.
lines.vis: The carrier, lit from below like a dungeon; Meatball picks it up anyway.

lines.say: In one British study, about one in five cats hadn't seen a vet in the year before their eighth birthday.
lines.vis: Five cats; one fades to an outline. Card: 1 IN 5

lines.say: Then there's the surgery. Getting fixed is one of the most common vet operations in the United States.
lines.vis: A vet clinic door; a cone of shame waits on a hook.

lines.say: In a small 1997 study, six neutered males gained about 30 percent in weight. Five intact males gained about 12.
lines.vis: Two cats on scales; one dial swings further. Card: +30% vs +12%

lines.say: But in British vet records, being neutered went with a longer life.
lines.vis: A timeline bar grows longer for the neutered cat.

lines.say: That's a link, not proof. Still: neutering can mean weight gain, and maybe more years. Hell of a trade.
lines.vis: The cat in a cone, wide, staring into the distance.

lines.say: And declawing. It's surgery, not a nail trim.
lines.vis: A nail clipper is pushed aside; a surgical tray slides in.

lines.say: New York banned it in 2019, except for medical reasons.
lines.vis: Card: NEW YORK, 2019: BANNED

lines.say: The law names three surgeries: declawing, phalangectomy and tendonectomy.
lines.vis: The bill text on a page with three terms underlined, spelled as the bill spells them: ONYCHECTOMY (DECLAWING), PHLANGECTOMY, TENDONECTOMY. No anatomy drawing.

lines.say: And studies are mixed on whether the pain lasts.
lines.vis: Two papers side by side with different verdict stamps.

lines.say: And all of that comes from the people who love you.
lines.vis: Meatball appears in the doorway with open arms.

lines.say: Number seven. Your human. He means well.
lines.vis: Chapter card; Meatball waves, far too close.

lines.say: He pets you. In two studies, cats reacted worst to being stroked near the tail.
lines.vis: A petting map of the cat: the tail end glows red. Card: TAIL END: WORST

lines.say: In one of them, the best-rated spot was between the eyes and the ears.
lines.vis: The same map: between eyes and ears glows green.

lines.say: He goes straight for the tail end. Every damn time.
lines.vis: Meatball's hand goes to the red zone; the cat's ears flatten. Character beat.

lines.say: Here's the rude part. In the 2015 study, cats showed more negative behaviour with a person they knew than with a stranger.
lines.vis: Two score bars under the heading NEGATIVE-BEHAVIOUR SCORE: FAMILIAR 8.5, STRANGER 5.0.

lines.say: The authors say it needs more research.
lines.vis: Meatball, wounded, hand on chest.

lines.say: He calls your name. You can probably tell it from other words.
lines.vis: Speech bubbles with random words; the cat's name bubble glows.

lines.say: In that test, over half of the cats just moved their ears or heads, name or not. Fewer than one in ten meowed.
lines.vis: One ear rotates toward the sound.

lines.say: But you get one win. The purr.
lines.vis: Close on the cat, eyes half shut.

lines.say: A 2009 study found that some cats, when they want food, add a high, cry-like sound to the purr.
lines.vis: A purr waveform; inside it, a smaller sharp wave is highlighted.

lines.say: People rated those purrs as more urgent and less pleasant. Even people who had never owned a cat.
lines.vis: Listeners with headphones wince and mark rating cards.

lines.say: Take the cry out, and the urgency ratings dropped.
lines.vis: The sharp wave is erased; the listeners relax.

lines.say: The university's news release says cats appear to be exploiting the human instinct to care for babies.
lines.vis: A baby-shaped silhouette fades over the cat.

lines.say: You may have hacked your damn human. Before breakfast. Enjoy it, because your body has plans.
lines.vis: Meatball fills the bowl at 5 AM in his pyjamas, hypnotised. Character beat.

lines.say: Number eight. Your own body.
lines.vis: Chapter card; the cat, older now, a little grey at the muzzle.

lines.say: The vets who write the pain guidelines say pain in cats has traditionally been under-recognised. The signs can be subtle.
lines.vis: The old cat sits very still; Meatball walks past without noticing.

lines.say: Here's what X-rays found. Researchers X-rayed 100 cats of all ages from one practice.
lines.vis: A light box; X-ray films slide in. Card: 100 CATS

lines.say: On X-ray, 92 of them had signs of joint disease.
lines.vis: Pause-and-reveal 3 of 3. Card: 92 OF 100: X-RAY SIGNS

lines.say: That's X-ray signs. It doesn't tell us how many were hurting.
lines.vis: The X-ray stays up; a small question mark next to a paw.

lines.say: Kidneys. The number depends on who you test and how.
lines.vis: Two clipboards.

lines.say: About 11 percent of older cats screened at two British clinics. About 77 percent of the senior cats staged at one American vet school, early stages counted.
lines.vis: Clipboard one: 11%. Clipboard two: 77% (EARLY STAGES COUNTED). Card: 11% OR 77%: DEPENDS HOW YOU COUNT

lines.say: And in that American study, the owners thought their cats were healthy.
lines.vis: Meatball gives a thumbs up next to the old cat.

lines.say: Of the cats with kidney disease, three in four owners had seen no change in their peeing.
lines.vis: Four litter boxes; at three of them Meatball shrugs: looks normal.

lines.say: And all 129 senior cats in the study had a dental problem. Every damn one.
lines.vis: The cat yawns: a dentist's mirror. Card: 129 OF 129: DENTAL

lines.say: Hairballs, at least, are honest. A Cornell vet says one every week or two is nothing to worry about.
lines.vis: A hairball lands on the rug with a tiny flag in it.

lines.say: Unless you get tired, stop eating for a day or two, or keep retching with nothing coming up. Then it's a vet, without delay.
lines.vis: The old cat lies flat by a full bowl; the carrier's shadow again. Card: TIRED, NOT EATING, RETCHING: VET

lines.say: So. Eight for eight. Raw as hell?
lines.vis: All eight chips filled; the meter sits at 24, blinking.

lines.say: Before you answer, look at what's waiting on the other side of the door.
lines.vis: The front door opens onto a street at dusk.

lines.say: Researchers followed more than 2,400 British pet cats for eight years. The study didn't record which ones went outside.
lines.vis: A long row of cat silhouettes. Card: 2,444 CATS, 8 YEARS

lines.say: Of the 362 cats that died, 165 died in road accidents. Almost half.
lines.vis: Headlights on a wet road; no impact shown. Card: ROADS: 165 OF 362 DEATHS

lines.say: For kittens under one, it was 41 of 67 deaths. 61 percent.
lines.vis: A kitten at the kerb; card: 41 OF 67 KITTEN DEATHS

lines.say: In one study of managed feral colonies, three in four kittens died or vanished before six months. Those are not pet-cat odds.
lines.vis: A colony behind a fence; four kitten outlines, three fade.
lines.card: FERAL COLONIES: 3 IN 4 GONE BY 6 MONTHS

lines.say: And the ASPCA estimates that about three million cats entered US shelters and rescues in 2025. About 277,000 were euthanized.
lines.vis: A shelter corridor; card: 2025: ABOUT 3 MILLION IN, 277,000 EUTHANIZED (ASPCA)

lines.say: The British researchers put it plainly. Keeping cats indoors can cut the road risk. But it may make a cat's behavioural needs harder to meet.
lines.vis: The door closes again; the cat watches the street through the screen.

lines.say: So here's the ledger.
lines.vis: The parchment from the cold open comes back, two columns.

lines.say: In British vet records, a newborn kitten can expect about eleven and three quarter years.
lines.vis: Card: 11.74 YEARS AT BIRTH (UK, 2019)

lines.say: In a second study of English cats that died, half made it past fourteen.
lines.vis: Card: HALF PASSED 14 (ENGLAND, 2009-12)

lines.say: That first table misses cats that died before a vet visit, which flatters it. Most deaths in it were euthanasia, which drags it down. Read it as a sketch.
lines.vis: A small-print footnote unrolls from the parchment.

lines.say: Guinness says the oldest cat ever lived 38 years and 3 days.
lines.vis: A very old cat with a party hat. Card: 38 YEARS (GUINNESS)

lines.say: Tough old badass.
lines.vis: The old cat blows out the candles in one go.

lines.say: And in that eight-year study of 2,400 British pet cats, the recorded chance of dying in any one year, up to age eight, was under four percent.
lines.vis: A small flat line labelled UNDER 4% A YEAR (AGES 0-8, MINIMUM).

lines.say: So a safe house could win on years. What it owes you is everything else.
lines.vis: The right column of the ledger is still empty.

lines.say: The cat vets' own guidelines call meeting your environmental needs essential, not optional.
lines.vis: Card: ESSENTIAL (NOT OPTIONAL)

lines.say: A safe place.
lines.vis: Pillar 1: the cat in a box on a high shelf.

lines.say: Your food, water, litter and scratching spots, kept apart.
lines.vis: Pillar 2: four stations around the room.

lines.say: Play that lets you hunt.
lines.vis: Pillar 3: Meatball drags a toy mouse; the cat pounces.

lines.say: Humans who are friendly and predictable.
lines.vis: Pillar 4: Meatball finally pets between the eyes and ears. Callback to the petting map.

lines.say: And a home that respects your nose.
lines.vis: Pillar 5: the cat rubs its cheek on the sofa corner.

lines.say: Get those, plus a safe house and vet visits, and the deal looks pretty damn sweet.
lines.vis: The meter climbs.

lines.say: Miss them, and it's a lot rawer. Free rent, though.
lines.vis: The meter dips, then steadies at 66.

lines.say: Thousands of years ago, a wildcat probably walked into a grain store for the mice.
lines.vis: CALLBACK: the wildcat in the doorway of the grain store, same framing as chapter 1.

lines.say: Cats have never left. Lucky bastards.
lines.vis: The wildcat lies down in the doorway; cross-fade to the house cat on the sofa in the same pose.

lines.say: Verdict: a sweet deal, if your human keeps the house safe and reads the damn manual.
lines.vis: Stamp: SWEET DEAL (IF...). Meatball holds a book titled THE MANUAL, upside down.

lines.say: Next time, you're born as something much bigger. This one's worth your time while you wait.
lines.vis: End screen: the next video tile; the cat's tail flicks over the tile.

pinned_comment: Raw deal or sweet deal? And what's the weirdest thing your cat does that this didn't explain?
end_screen_video: best for viewer (the next 'born as' episode when it exists)
_factcheck: research/88-factcheck-house-cat-script.md applied 2026-11-12 (two rounds; the checker's last word: safe to build): about 45 lines softened or re-attributed; two fact-pack misreads fixed (kidney share is 77% of staged cats, not 61%; 109 of 119 fallen cats lived, not 96.5%); the declaw sponsor-memo line replaced by the bill's own wording. Title 1 has 'sucks': needs Nolan's yes before it is used.
